situation.note: I failed my bank exam for the fourth time. the whole village knows. my father has stopped going to the chaupal because people ask about me.

understanding.bridge: The village is talking about you, but the one who cannot stop going over it is your own mind, and the Gita says that is the real enemy.
understanding.core_struggle: After failing a bank exam four times, the whole village knows and his father has withdrawn from the chaupal; he cannot stop replaying it.
understanding.mirror: You keep going over the same failure, and the village is talking about it.
understanding.insight: You replayed the failure last night. Underneath is the belief that the whole village's verdict is the truth of you.

I can't let go of resentment

queries.hook: The weight of a failure everyone knows, and the shame that has reached your father, replayed in your mind until you cannot sleep. My project or startup failed.
queries.diagnose: When a result goes wrong, the mind turns against itself; self-blame grows from believing the outcome alone measures our worth, and it grows in the silence of the chaupal.
queries.steady: A failure is something that happened, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost, and your father's love is not measured by the exam.
queries.act: Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; learn what this taught you, make amends where you can, and begin again.
queries.story: A man who failed again and again, faced the village's silence and his own shame, yet found the courage to rise again.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verse.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verse.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verse.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

matched.label: I feel guilty about something I did

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that if someone thinks they are the sole cause of success or failure, they are not seeing the whole picture. Every action has five causes: the setting, the person acting, the tools used, the effort made, and what comes from outside. Seeing yourself as the only one who made something happen, or the only one who caused it to fail, misses the full reality.
verse.for_you: The whole village knows about the exam, and your father has stopped going to the chaupal. You are carrying the weight of four failures, but your mind is telling you that you alone caused all of it.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you blame yourself alone for a small thing today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your own mind, holding the whole weight of the village's eyes.
asks: What are the other four causes of my exam failing?
How do I separate my effort from the result?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Rama, near the end of his lament, says where the real enemy lives.
verse.sanskrit: शत्रवश्चेन्द्रियाण्येव सत्यं यातमसत्यताम् । प्रहरत्यात्मनैवात्मा मनसैव मनो रिपुः ॥
verse.line: No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy.
verse.translation: Our own senses are the enemies; truth itself has turned untrue; the self strikes the self, and the mind is the mind's own enemy.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
verse.misuse: Not a reason to blame yourself. Vasishtha's answer is that the same mind can lift itself.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.meaning: Rama, after losing his kingdom, asks the sage Vasishtha what the point of life is. He lists all the ways the world disappoints, how desire never ends, and how time takes everything. In the middle of this grief, he names the one enemy that is always inside us. He sees that our own senses and thoughts turn against us. They make us attack our own peace. The truth begins to feel false, and the mind becomes its own worst enemy.
verse.for_you: The village is talking, but the one who is replaying the failure is your own mind, and that is the real enemy. Your thoughts are not the village. They are the echo. You can listen to them without believing them.
verse.try_today: Name one thought that is not true today.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own lament, and the mind is its own enemy.
asks: How do I stop the mind from being my own enemy?
Can the mind that hurts me also heal me?
Who is the good company I need right now?

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: पुत्र नात्मावमन्तव्यः पूर्वाभिरसमृद्धिभिः / अभूत्वा हि भवन्त्यर्था भूत्वा नश्यन्ति चापरे / अमर्षेणैव चाप्यर्था नारब्धव्याः सुबालिशैः
verse.line: Don't look down on yourself because of past failures. Fortunes come and go, and can come again.
verse.translation: Son, don't look down on yourself because of past failures. Fortunes that never were come to be, and fortunes that were are lost. But don't start things out of mere resentment, like a fool.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: A mistake is something you did, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
verse.line: The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
verse.translation: The steady person whom these do not disturb, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for immortality.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Steadiness is not numbness or hiding what you feel.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the person who remains steady in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom. These feelings come and go like the seasons. They touch the body, but they do not touch the self. The one who understands this is not shaken by sorrow or swept away by joy. They have found the center that does not move.
verse.for_you: The village knows, and that is pain. But the one who cannot stop replaying it is your own mind. That is the real trouble. Your mind is becoming your own enemy. You are not seeing the whole picture. You think you alone made it fail. But fortunes come and go.
verse.try_today: Notice when the replay starts, and name it as a season, not a truth.
verse.scene_line: You are standing in your own waiting room, watching the seasons of shame pass through.
asks: How do I see the whole picture without my own mind in it?
Can I let the failure be a season and not a verdict?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verse.sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
verse.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
verse.translation: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
verse.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that knowledge is the way out of confusion. It is not learned by arguing or showing off. It is learned by approaching someone who knows, with humility and respect. You ask them real questions. You serve them. The wise ones who have seen the truth will then teach you. This knowledge is powerful. It can carry even someone who has done terrible things across to safety. To get it, you need faith and self-control. Doubt is the thing that destroys everything. So you could cut your doubt and stand up.
verse.for_you: Your mind is replaying the exam failure because you believe the village's verdict is the truth of you. But you can learn a different truth from those who have seen it. Approach your own experience with humility and ask what it is really teaching you.
verse.try_today: Ask one real question about why you failed, without judging the answer.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own chaupal, waiting for the village verdict to end.
asks: What is the real question I am avoiding?
Who in my life can teach me without judgment?
How do I serve the process instead of my pride?

verse.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verse.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verse.sanskrit: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः
verse.line: Turn to doing good after a wrong, and you come out like the moon from behind a cloud.
verse.translation: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
verse.why: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

prasang.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
prasang.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
prasang.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

verse.for_you: Be on your own side: lift yourself up, make amends where you can, and begin again; no one who does good is lost.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

prasang.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
prasang.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
prasang.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

story.hook_title: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.teaser: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.for_you: The village is talking. You are holding back from your own leap because you are listening to a verdict that is not true. You have the strength, the brains and the courage.
asks: How do I know the verdict is not true?
How do I stop listening to the village?
What does my own leap look like today?
